newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GWYNN MAKES SUCCESSFUL RETURN TO PADRES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GWYNN MAKES SUCCESSFUL RETURN TO PADRES.

text.p: Tony Gwynn celebrated his return to the lineup following a battle with kidney stones by collecting two hits and driving in the winning run Thursday night as the San Diego Padres edged the Cincinnati Reds 5-4.

Mandy Romero led off the bottom of the 10th against Reds closer Jeff Shaw (3-2) with a single and was sacrificed to second. Quilvio Veras beat out an infield hit to put runners on first and third and Gwynn, playing his first game since last Friday, followed with a slow roller to second that the Reds couldn't convert into a double play.

"I was actually swinging the bat pretty well," Gwynn said of his final at-bat. "As soon as I hit the ball I thought it would get up the middle...All the way down I was watching (Ed) Perez's glove to see if he was stretching for a throw."
"I wasn't trying to strike him out," Shaw said of Gwynn. "I was just trying for a double play. Trying to strike him out is like banging your head against a wall."
Perez and Jon Nunnally belted solo homers in the top of the eighth to give Cincinnati a 4-3 lead, but Shaw couldn't hold it.

Ken Caminiti led off the ninth for the Padres with a double and moved to third on a groundout. After pinch-hitter Steve Finley grounded out, Wally Joyner batted for Archi Cianfrocco and lined the first pitch into the right-center field gap to send the game into extra innings.
"I was just missing pitches I should be hitting all day," Caminiti said. "I'm just very happy to contribute offensively."
Trevor Hoffman (5-4), who tossed a scoreless 10th, earned the victory.
Gwynn doubled home a run in the third inning and was on base when Greg Vaughn hit his 13th homer in the sixth.
In Los Angeles, Ismael Valdes allowed four hits over 8 1/3 innings and Mike Piazza belted his 26th home run in the third inning to lead the Dodgers to a 1-0 victory over the Montreal Expos.

Valdes (7-10) walked one and struck out five in equaling his longest outing of the season and outdueling Expos ace Pedro Martinez. It was Valdez's seventh straight start in which he allowed three runs or less.

Montreal first baseman David Segui was robbed of home runs by center fielder Otis Nixon in the second and fourth innings. Nixon leaped over the wall to rob Segui of a solo shot in the second inning and took away another homer in the fourth with one man aboard.
In San Francisco, Bill Mueller had three hits, including a three-run homer, and Shawn Estes struck out 10 batters in 7 1/3 innings, lifting the Giants to a 7-3 victory over the Chicago Cubs.
Estes (15-4) yielded two runs, five hits and walked three as he fanned 10 for the second consecutive outing. His 15 wins are the most by a Giants left-hander since Vida Blue registered 18 in 1978.
"My goal at the start of the season was to win 15," Estes said. "Dusty (Giants manager Dusty Baker) says don't stop there, so I won't set any more goals. Each game is real important for us now."
The Giants lead the National League West by 1 1/2 games over Los Angeles, and they already have matched their 1996 wins total with 68.
Mueller's three hits came in his first three at-bats and gave him six straight hits going back to Tuesday.

In St. Louis, Bobby Jones allowed two runs over seven innings to win for the first time in nearly two months and Edgardo Alfonzo hit his first career grand slam as the New York Mets beat the Cardinals, 6-2.

Jones (13-7) allowed only a two-run homer to Delino DeShields and six singles, walking two and striking out two. The first pitcher in the major leagues to record 12 victories, Jones won for the first time since June 20. In winning for the first time in nine starts, he also established a career high in victories.

Turk Wendell and Greg McMichael combined on a scoreless eighth and Mel Rojas tossed a perfect ninth to preserve the win, which moved the Mets within 2 1/2 games of idle Florida in the National League wild-card race.
Alfonzo, 11-for-24 lifetime in bases-loaded situations, staked the Mets to a 5-0 lead in the fifth when he crushed a 1-2 pitch from Donovan Osborne over the left-field wall.
